title: Cate's First Day
description: An A2 reading and writing module about Cate’s first day as an exchange student in Glasgow. Explain eight travel words and phrases in English, use them in your own sentences and practise simple past questions and negatives.

competencies.description: Practice focus: understand the main events, reasons and feelings in a connected A2 story.
Practice focus: write English explanations, meaningful example sentences, questions and a short diary entry; check open answers with examples.
Practice focus: explain eight travel words and phrases in English and use them in meaningful contexts.
Practice focus: use simple past questions and negatives with did/did not and was/were, including base forms of regular and irregular verbs.

learningObjectives: I can understand Cate’s first-day story, explain eight travel words and phrases in English and use each one in a meaningful sentence.
I can ask and answer simple past questions, make negative sentences with did not and was/were not, and write a short diary entry as Cate.

blocks.title: Help Cate tell her story
blocks.body:
Cate, the EveryCate learning robot, is spending an exchange year at the **University of Glasgow**. Her first day brings a broken screen, helpful strangers and an unexpected surprise. Read her story, investigate the language and help her write her diary.

You already know regular verbs with **-ed**, irregular past forms and **did/didn't**. Here you will use them to explain events and ask better questions.

**Your learning goals:**

- I can understand Cate’s first-day story, explain eight travel words and phrases in English and use each one in a meaningful sentence.
- I can ask and answer simple past questions, make negative sentences with did not and was/were not, and write a short diary entry as Cate.

You can complete every activity by reading and writing.

blocks.title: Words to investigate
blocks.body:
Find these eight words and phrases in the story. Notice **what they mean** and **how Cate uses them**. The German meanings can help you get started; later you will explain each meaning in English and create your own examples.

**journey** – eine Reise

**railway station** – Bahnhof

**ticket** – Fahrkarte

**passenger** – eine Person, die in einem Verkehrsmittel mitreist

**friendly** – freundlich

**nearby** – in der Nähe

**over there** – dort drüben

**diary** – Tagebuch

Learn **railway station** and **over there** as whole phrases. When you explain a word, give useful information: *a person who …*, *a place where …*, *something you use to …* or *it means …*.

blocks.title: A difficult arrival, a good surprise
blocks.body:
**Read Cate’s account of yesterday. How did her feelings change during the day?**

Yesterday I travelled to Glasgow to start my exchange year at the University of Glasgow. My journey was long because the train arrived twenty minutes late. I was a passenger with two bags and a screen full of useful information. My ticket and the address of my student accommodation were on it. During the journey, the ticket inspector checked my ticket, so everything seemed fine.

However, when I got off at a small railway station near Glasgow, my screen suddenly went dark. I didn't have a paper map, and I didn't know which exit to use. Two students, Calum and Timo, noticed me near the doors. ‘Did you lose your ticket?’ Calum asked. ‘No, I didn't. My screen stopped working,’ I explained. They were friendly, but I felt embarrassed because I needed help on my very first day.

Timo opened a map on his phone. I remembered the name of my accommodation, and he found it quickly. It was nearby, so we didn't take a bus. ‘It's over there, behind the café,’ he said. We walked there together. When we compared our room numbers, we discovered that we were flatmates!

Calum is from Scotland, and Timo is an exchange student from Germany who studies engineering. In our flat, each bedroom has its own bathroom, but we share a kitchen. I was surprised when Calum carried his expensive bike into his bedroom. He explained that he was worried about thieves, so he didn't leave it outside.

Timo lent me a charger, and soon my screen worked again. That evening, we didn't go to a restaurant. We cooked pasta in our shared kitchen and talked about our plans. My first day wasn't easy, but I wasn't alone either. Now my diary is open. How can I explain the problem, the help and the surprise in just a few sentences?

**Reading help:** ticket inspector = a person who checks passengers’ tickets; exit = a way out of a building; embarrassed = uncomfortable because you think you look silly; accommodation = a place where you stay; flatmates = people who share a flat; engineering = designing and building things such as machines; thieves = people who steal things; lent = the past form of lend, to give someone something to use and return later; charger = something that gives power to a battery.

blocks.title: Events, reasons and feelings
blocks.intro: Choose the best answer. Find the sentence or sentences that support your choice. After a mistake, read the explanation and try again.

questions.prompt: Why did Cate need help at the railway station?

options.text: Her screen stopped working, so she could not read the address or map.
The ticket inspector took her screen away.
She left both bags on the train.

questions.explanation: The address was on her screen. It went dark, and she had no paper map. Connect the information in the first two paragraphs and try again.

questions.prompt: How did Timo help Cate find the accommodation?

options.text: He told her to take a bus because it was far away.
He found it on his phone after she remembered its name.
He read the address from her working screen.

questions.explanation: Cate remembered the name, and Timo found it on his phone. Her own screen was still dark. Read the third paragraph before trying again.

questions.prompt: Why did the three students walk to the accommodation?

options.text: They wanted to leave the city.
They did not know where the accommodation was.
It was nearby, so they did not need a bus.

questions.explanation: “It was nearby, so we didn’t take a bus.” The word so connects the short distance with their decision to walk. Try again if needed.

questions.prompt: Why did Calum put his bike in his bedroom?

options.text: He wanted to protect it from thieves.
He planned to cook with it in the kitchen.
He wanted to lend it to the ticket inspector.

questions.explanation: Calum was worried about thieves. Keeping the expensive bike inside made him feel safer. Look for the reason in the fourth paragraph.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best describes Cate’s day?

options.text: She felt confident at first, but her flatmates refused to help.
She felt embarrassed at the station, but later she had help and company.
She was alone all day and never found the accommodation.

questions.explanation: At the station Cate felt embarrassed. Later Timo lent her a charger, and the students cooked and talked together. Use both parts of the story when you try again.

blocks.title: Explain the meaning in English
blocks.intro: Match each word or phrase to its English explanation. After a mistake, use these clues: passenger describes a person; friendly describes behaviour; nearby describes distance; over there points to a place. Read the story or word bank again, then retry.

rechts.text: a trip from one place to another, for example by train
a place where trains stop so that people can get on or off
a paper or digital pass that allows you to travel on a bus, train or another vehicle
a person who travels in a vehicle but does not drive it
kind and pleasant towards other people
not far away from a place
in that place, away from where the speaker is, often shown by pointing
a book or digital record where someone writes about daily events and feelings

blocks.title: Your explanations and examples
blocks.intro: For each target word, write a short English explanation in your own words and then a meaningful example sentence. Try without looking at the matching activity first. You may use a new, imagined situation for your examples. Explain the meaning instead of only translating into German. Open the hint if you get stuck. Compare with the sample afterwards; many different answers are possible.

tasks.prompt:
**journey**

**Explain:** What does it mean? Use English without repeating the target word as its own explanation.

**Use:** Write your own complete sentence with **journey**. Add a detail that makes the meaning clear. For example, “It was nearby” needs a place and a clue about the distance.
tasks.hint: Explain what happens between leaving one place and arriving at another.
tasks.solution:
**Possible explanation:** a trip from one place to another, for example by train.

**Possible example:** Our journey to the coast took three hours because the roads were busy.

**Self-check:** Is my explanation in English and accurate? Does my example use the whole word or phrase naturally? Is there enough context to understand it? A different clear explanation or example is also valid. Revise your answer if needed.

tasks.hint: Describe the place and say what people do there. You can use the word trains.
tasks.solution:

blocks.title: Ask and correct: simple past
blocks.body:
You already know past forms such as **walked, noticed, went** and **took**. Focus on what changes when you ask a question or make a sentence negative.

| Statement | Yes/no question | Negative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| They walked there. | **Did** they **walk** there? | They **didn’t walk** there. |
| Cate took a bus. | **Did** Cate **take** a bus? | Cate **didn’t take** a bus. |
| Her screen was dark. | **Was** her screen dark? | Her screen **wasn’t** dark. |
| The students were outside. | **Were** the students outside? | The students **weren’t** outside. |

These are grammar examples; check the story for what really happened.

With most verbs, use **did + person + base form** for a question and **person + didn’t + base form** for a negative. The past is already in did, so use **go**, not went; **help**, not helped. **didn’t = did not**.

For a question with a question word: **Where/Why/What + did + person + base form …?**

- Where **did** they **cook**? – In the shared kitchen.
- Why **did** they **walk**? – Because the accommodation was nearby.

With **be**, use **was/were** directly: **Was** Cate worried? **Were** her flatmates helpful? Use **wasn’t / was not** or **weren’t / were not** for negatives. Do not add did to was/were.

**Short answers:** Did Timo help? – Yes, he **did**. / No, he **didn’t**. Was the journey long? – Yes, it **was**. / No, it **wasn’t**.

blocks.title: Build yes/no and wh-questions
blocks.intro: Complete each question with did and the base form of the verb in brackets. You know the past forms, but questions need the base form. If you make a mistake, check the verb after did and try again.
blocks.text:
{{1}} Cate {{2}} by train? (travel)
{{3}} she {{4}} her ticket? (lose)
What {{5}} Timo {{6}} on his phone? (open)
Why {{7}} they {{8}} to the accommodation? (walk)
Where {{9}} Calum {{10}} his bike? (put)
What {{11}} Timo {{12}} Cate? (lend)

blocks.title: Correct the false claims
blocks.intro: Each claim below is false. Change it into a negative sentence that matches the story. Use did not or didn’t and the base form of the verb in the claim. After a mistake, check both parts: did not + base form, then try again.
blocks.text:
Claim: Cate lost her ticket.
Correction: Cate {{1}} {{2}} her ticket.

Claim: The students took a bus to the accommodation.
Correction: The students {{3}} {{4}} a bus to the accommodation.

Claim: Calum left his bike outside.
Correction: Calum {{5}} {{6}} his bike outside.

Claim: The students went to a restaurant that evening.
Correction: The students {{7}} {{8}} to a restaurant that evening.

Claim: Timo ignored Cate at the station.
Correction: Timo {{9}} {{10}} Cate at the station.

blocks.title: Questions and negatives with be
blocks.intro: Complete the questions and statements with was, were, wasn’t or weren’t. Full negative forms are also accepted. Match the story. Hint: Cate / screen / accommodation = she or it; the students = they. Use be directly, without did. Then retry any mistakes.
blocks.text:
{{1}} Cate embarrassed at the station?
{{2}} Calum and Timo friendly?
The screen {{3}} bright at the station; it was dark.
The accommodation {{4}} far away; it was nearby.
The students {{5}} in a restaurant that evening; they were in their kitchen.

blocks.title: Answer from the story
blocks.intro: Complete each short answer using information from the story. You can use short or full negative forms. Hint: an answer to Did …? uses did/didn’t; an answer to Was/Were …? uses a form of be. Check and retry if needed.
blocks.text:
Did Cate lose her ticket? No, she {{1}}.
Did Timo lend Cate a charger? Yes, he {{2}}.
Was the accommodation far away? No, it {{3}}.
Were Calum and Timo friendly? Yes, they {{4}}.

blocks.title: Spot and repair the mistake
blocks.intro: Choose the correctly repaired sentence. Explain the change to yourself before checking. Use the feedback to improve your next attempt.

options.text: Did Cate travelled by train?
Did Cate travel by train?
Was Cate travel by train?

questions.explanation: After did, use the base form travel. Did already marks the past. The same rule applies to regular verbs with -ed. Try again if needed.

questions.prompt: Repair: “Calum didn’t left his bike outside.”

options.text: Calum didn’t leave his bike outside.
Calum didn’t left his bike outside.
Calum wasn’t leave his bike outside.

questions.explanation: The base form of left is leave. After didn’t, use leave, even though left is an irregular past form. Read the whole correction and retry.

questions.prompt: Repair: “Did the students were in the kitchen?”

options.text: Did the students be in the kitchen?
Was the students in the kitchen?
Were the students in the kitchen?

questions.explanation: For be, move were to the front and do not add did. The students = they, so were is the right form. Try again if needed.

blocks.title: Interview Cate in writing
blocks.intro: Now build whole questions yourself. Write the questions and answers in the answer box, then compare with the examples. Different questions are welcome if the answers match the story.

tasks.prompt:
Imagine you are writing an interview with Cate for a student website. Write **three questions** and **Cate’s answers**:

- One yes/no question with **did**.
- One question starting with **Where** or **Why** and using **did**.
- One question with **was** or **were**.

Write at least **one full negative sentence** in Cate’s answers. Address Cate as **you**; she answers with **I** or **we**. Use the story as your evidence.
tasks.hint:
Question starters: Did you …? / Where did you …? / Why did you …? / Were you …?

Answer starters: Yes, I did. / No, I didn’t. / I didn’t … because … / We … because …

Remember: did + base form. For be, move was/were to the front. An answer must fit both the question and the story.
tasks.solution:
**One possible interview:**

Did you take a bus to the accommodation? – No, I didn’t take a bus because it was nearby.

Where did you cook dinner? – We cooked pasta in our shared kitchen.

Were you embarrassed at the station? – Yes, I was, because I needed help.

**Self-check:** Do I have all three question types? Did I use a base form after did/didn’t? Is there a full negative sentence? Do the answers match the questions and the story? Different correct questions and answers are valid.

blocks.title: Write Cate’s diary
blocks.intro: Bring the vocabulary and grammar together. Write as Cate, then use the example and checklist to improve your text.

tasks.prompt:
Write **three connected diary sentences about yesterday** as Cate. Include the problem and how someone helped.

Use **at least three different target words or phrases**, **at least two correct forms of was/were** and **one negative with didn’t + base form**. Join ideas with **and, but, because** or **so** at least once. Your details must match the story.

A repeated correct form of was/were is fine. railway station and over there each count as one phrase. Keep the focus on yesterday.
tasks.hint:
Word bank: journey · railway station · ticket · passenger · friendly · nearby · over there · diary.

Sentence starters: My journey was … / At the railway station, I didn’t … / Timo … because … / Our accommodation was …, so …

You can use regular and irregular past forms in statements. After didn’t, use the base form. Open the story again if you need help with the facts.
tasks.solution:
**One possible entry:**

My journey was long, and I didn’t know which exit to use. A friendly student called Timo showed me a map at the railway station. Our accommodation was nearby, so we walked there together.

This entry uses **journey, friendly, railway station** and **nearby**. It uses **was** twice, **didn’t know**, and the linking words **and** and **so**.

**Self-check:**

- Three complete sentences, written as Cate about yesterday?
- At least three different target words or whole phrases used naturally?
- At least two correct forms of was/were and one didn’t + base form?
- Ideas linked with and, but, because or so?
- Both the problem and the help included, with details that match the story?

Other clear, accurate texts are valid. The example is for comparison, not the only correct answer. Ask your teacher if you are unsure.

blocks.title: Quick check
blocks.intro: Try without the word bank or grammar table first. These are new practice situations, not extra facts about Cate’s story. Use the verbs in brackets. After a mistake, check the base form after did/didn’t or the plural subject with were, then try again.

tasks.prompt:
Choose one statement for **vocabulary** and one for **simple past questions and negatives**:

- I can do this already
- I did it with help
- I want to practise this more

For vocabulary, think about explaining the words in English and using them in meaningful sentences. For grammar, think about did/didn’t + base form and questions with was/were. Add one example from your work to explain your choices.
tasks.hint: Could someone understand your explanations without a German translation? Do your examples make the meanings clear? Can you write a whole question and a negative without copying the model?
tasks.solution: There is no right or wrong choice. For example: “Vocabulary: I did it with help. The sentence about walking for two minutes helped me explain nearby.” Pick one explanation or one grammar answer to improve next.
